conditions: Description headed 'Male (holotype).' of the only species of the monotypic new genus Paleotoca. Type material as printed: 'Holotype male and female paratype from Cave AP-0038 (Paleoburrow)', Caeté, Minas Gerais, Brazil, 12 February 2012, R. Andrade et al. leg., 'deposited in IBSP 264705'; further paratypes from the same cave, 1♀ (IBSP 264708), 1♂ (19-25 July 2008, IBSP 264704) and 2♀ (31 May to 5 June 2012, IBSP 264707); other material 3♀ and 1♂ from caves AP-0069, AP-0065 (Caeté), FN-0019 (Mariana) and APOL-0001 (Santa Bárbara). Distribution: 'known only from ferruginous caves in Quadrilátero Ferrífero'. The same absence is printed for the female ('Female (paratype).' ... 'Eye absent.') and for the genus ('Eyes absent'). No eye measurement; Methods: 'All measurements are in millimeters.'

source.authors: Cizauskas I, Zampaulo RA, Brescovit AD
source.title: A New Genus of Prodidominae Cave Spider from a Paleoburrow and Ferruginous Caves in Brazil (Araneae: Prodidomidae)

where: Section 3.3, male description of Paleotoca diminas
note: The sentence does not repeat the species name; it sits under the male holotype description of the only species. The Remarks call it 'a troglobitic spider with reduction in cuticular pigments, eye absent, heavy spination and trichobothria', the Abstract lists 'eye loss', and the Discussion says 'Body depigmentation, anophthalmia and sensory organs (e.g., trichobrotria) are autapomorphies related to the way of life of this spider, specialized in the subterranean environment [16].' No vestigial or reduced-eye qualifier anywhere in the paper. eyes_count 0 for 'Eyes absent.' follows main (Coecobrya, desk-d293; Leptonetela arvanitidisi, desk-d283; audit 464 ruling that eyes_count 0 and eye_type none are both in use). Not on main (audit 470 grep of the whole docs/ tree for Paleotoca, diminas, taxonomy4030028, 4030028: only a false hit on the author name Gediminas in wanted lists). Name and family (audit 470): the World Spider Catalog page was not reached; the Wikipedia Prodidomidae article says the family 'was formerly regarded as a subfamily of Gnaphosidae, but was raised to a family in 2022' and lists 'Paleotoca Cizauskas, Zampaulo & Brescovit, 2024 – Brazil'; the paper prints Prodidomidae and 'Composition. Monotypic.'
